name: Dyschromatosis Symmetrica Hereditaria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Dyschromatosis Symmetrica Hereditaria

criteria.description: Presence of both hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules distributed symmetrically on the dorsal aspects of the hands and feet
Onset of skin lesions typically in infancy or early childhood
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Lack of systemic symptoms or involvement of internal organs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetrical hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules on extremities with onset in early childhood; family history supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ADAR gene mutations can support diagnosis but is not required

imaging: Not typically indicated; no characteristic imaging findings
genetic: Mutations in ADAR gene (adenosine deaminase acting on RNA) associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Histopathology shows basal layer hyperpigmentation, pigment incontinence, and mild epidermal atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized distribution of pigmentation abnormalities including trunk and limbs
Photosensitivity with early onset skin cancers
Atrophic, angulated hyperpigmented macules primarily on the dorsal hands
Histology shows epidermal atrophy and basal layer hyperpigmentation

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms (neurological or immunological)
Presence of skin ulcerations or suspicious lesions suggestive of malignancy
references: Happle R. Dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria: clinical and genetic aspects. Dermatol Clin. 1995;13(3):475-482.
Zhao Y, et al. ADAR mutations in dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria. J Invest Dermatol. 2013;133(2): 505-508.
